summary: Sherry Chayat is a Buddhist studies scholar. She studied at Vassar College and trained under the traditional teacher Eido Shimano.

Shi Hu (1891–1962) was a scholar of philosophy, sinology, and history and archaeology. He studied at National University, Cornell, and Columbia under John Dewey, later serving at Peking University (~1917–1948) and leading Academia Sinica (1958–1962).

Shichang Ma (1934–2018) worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He was a Buddhist archaeology researcher at the Dunhuang Academy (1963–1978) and joined the Archaeology Department at Peking University in 1982, where he taught Giuseppe Vignato.
Shigeki Kaizuka (1904–1987) was a sinologist, historian, and archaeologist. He studied at Kyoto University from ~1925 to 1928 and later held a post there from ~1931 to 1968.

Shigeki Kudo (b. 1931) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as an assistant at Kyoto University, an assistant professor at Shitennoji University (attested 1972–1973), and an assistant professor at Shuchiin University.

Shigeki Moro works in Buddhist studies, computational fields, and philosophy. He studied at Waseda, Toyo, and Kansai universities under Ryoshun Okubo and Koyu Tamura, later holding posts at Hanazono University and becoming a professor at Waseda University in 2025.
Shigemasa Fukui (b. 1935) specializes in sinology, history, and archaeology. He completed his studies at Waseda University (~1955–1965) and later served as a professor there from ~1980 to 2006.

Shigemitsu Dando (1913–2012) studied under Seiichiro Ono at the University of Tokyo (~1932–1935). He held a post at the University of Tokyo (~1937–1974), taught briefly at Keio University (~1974), and served on the Supreme Court of Japan (~1974–1983).

Shigenori Nagatomo is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Temple University, where he is attested as professor of religious studies in 1999 and again in 2017, teaching Kin Cheung and Tao Jiang.

Shigeo Kamata (1927–2001) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Komazawa University under Kodo Sawaki and at the University of Tokyo, later serving at the University of Tokyo, Matsugaoka Bunko, and Aichi Gakuin University.

Shigeo Yokoyama (b. 1954) specializes in religious studies and related fields. He studied at Kyoto University from ~1973 to 1982, later holding academic posts at Okayama University (~1984–1992) and Nara Women's University (~1992–2020).

Shigeru Gorai (1908–1993) worked in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University, and later held posts at Otani University (1955–1978) and the Institute of Japanese Religious Folklore (~1974–1993).
Shigeru Kato (1880–1946) was a scholar in sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1902 to 1905 and later held a post there from ~1925 to 1941.

Shigeru Matsumoto (1933–2010) was a religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1953–1960) and Harvard University (~1960–1967), and later held posts at the University of the Sacred Heart (~1971–1980) and Tenri University (~1980–2003).

Shih-Hsiang Chen (1912–1971) was a sinologist who studied at Peking University (~1928–1932). He served on the faculty at the University of California, Berkeley from ~1945 to 1971, where he taught Gary Snyder.
Shikaripur N. Sridhar is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. At Stony Brook University, he has served as Chair (attested 2007) and as Director of the Center for India Studies (attested 2026).
Shikazo Mori (1906–1980) was a scholar of sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1927–1930) and later held an academic post at Bukkyo University (~1970–1978).

Shili Xiong (1885–1968) was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and sinology who studied under Jian Ouyang at the China Institute of Inner Learning. He held posts at Boone University, Zhejiang University, and Peking University (1923–1955).

Shilpa Sumant is an Indologist. She served as an editor and Regulating Council member at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (2020–2025) and is attested as a member at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute in 2026.

Shimei Futabatei (1864–1909) studied at Senshu College, Tokyo School of Foreign Languages, and Hitotsubashi University. Working in linguistics and other fields, he taught at the Tokyo School of Foreign Languages, military colleges, and worked for Asahi Shimbun.
